explain.say: See the bird? Birds ate more of the pale moths. The dark moths survived, bred and passed on the gene for dark wings. This is natural selection: the best-suited survive and have young. Can you say it in your own words?

faq.q: Why were some peppered moths dark?
faq.a: A mutation in one gene made some moths almost black. The mutation happened by chance; it was not caused by the soot.
asks: Tell me about pale and dark moths

faq.q: What did soot do to the trees?
faq.a: Smoke from burning coal killed the pale lichens on tree bark and coated it with black soot, so the bark became dark.
asks: Tell me about soot on the trees

faq.q: Why did birds eat more pale moths?
faq.a: On dark, sooty bark the pale moths were easy to see, while dark moths were camouflaged. Birds found and ate the pale ones more often.
asks: Tell me about birds spotting pale moths

faq.a: Living things vary. Those whose features suit their environment best are more likely to survive and reproduce, passing on their genes. Over many generations, those features become more common.

faq.q: What happened after the air got cleaner?
faq.a: After clean air laws, such as the UK Clean Air Act of 1956, soot decreased and lichens returned. Pale moths had the advantage again, and dark moths became rare.
asks: Are dark peppered moths still common?

facts: The first dark peppered moth was recorded in Manchester in 1848; by 1895 about 98% of moths there were dark.
In 2016, scientists traced the dark form to a mutation in a gene called cortex.

quiz.say: Why did dark peppered moths become common in sooty areas?
quiz.show: Why did dark peppered moths become common in sooty areas?

options.show: Birds ate more pale moths, so dark ones survived to breed
options.say: Birds ate more pale moths, so dark ones survived to breed

quiz.why: Natural selection: the camouflaged dark moths survived and passed on their genes.

wrong.0: Soot does not change a moth's genes; the dark form came from a chance mutation.
wrong.2: Animals cannot choose their genes; variation arises by chance.

quiz.say: What made the dark moths rarer again in the late 1900s?
quiz.show: What made the dark moths rarer again in the late 1900s?
quiz.why: Cleaner air meant paler bark, so pale moths were camouflaged again.

wrong.1: More birds would not favour one colour unless the bark changed.
wrong.2: The change matched falling pollution, not the weather.
